name: Fast Matrix Multiplications for Lookup Table-Quantized LLMs
problem: Non-uniform lookup-table quantization at awkward bit widths (e.g. 3 bits) makes the dequant and matmul kernel slow, which can eat the entire bandwidth saving.
mechanism: FLUTE is a kernel, not a format: offline RESTRUCTURING of the quantized weight matrix to minimize bit-manipulation work during unpacking, plus vectorization and DUPLICATION of the lookup table so shared-memory bandwidth is not the bottleneck. Offline restructuring is the trick - the deployment-time kernel becomes cheaper because of work done once at quantization time.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): at batch sizes < 32 and quantization group size 128 - the regime the paper correctly identifies as typical LLM inference - the FLUTE kernel is 2-4x FASTER THAN EXISTING GEMM KERNELS, because weight movement rather than arithmetic is the bottleneck. The compression ratio is whatever the underlying LUT format is (3-bit here); the quality cost belongs to the format, not to FLUTE. The honest reading: this is a single-sequence-decode kernel win, and the batch-size ceiling is explicit.
